articles.title: Iran says meeting with Mecca pact states will mark beginning of 'real transformation'
articles.summary:
Iran says meeting with Mecca pact states will mark beginning of 'real transformation'

Senior officials from the Mecca Defence Alliance met Iranian leaders in Tehran on Monday, with Iran’s top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, saying the talks showed US threats had little impact on regional diplomacy and would mark the start of a “real transformation”.

Members of the alliance, which includes Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, gathered in Tehran to negotiate as regional powers strive to end the Israeli-US war against Iran and establish a security framework independent of Washington.

The talks come as the conflict continues to threaten the region and the global economy, amid mounting fears of renewed Israeli-US attacks.

articles.title: ‘We left with heavy hearts’: Israel’s assault displaces thousands in Hebron
articles.summary:
‘We left with heavy hearts’: Israel’s assault displaces thousands in Hebron

Less than two weeks before her wedding, Mayar Amrish sat with her family in the spacious courtyard of their home, making plans for the big day.

The 23-year-old Palestinian was preparing for her future, but within hours, her family home would be reduced to rubble.

Outside the house in Farsh al-Hawa, in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron, Israeli forces were launching a sweeping demolition and forced displacement campaign.

The assault, condemned as collective punishment against Palestinians, followed a shooting on Friday in which two Palestinians killed two Israeli soldiers.

Israel imposed a total lockdown on the city and launched a wide-ranging military assault involving home raids, arrests, demolitions and the forced displacement of thousands of people.

Read more: ‘We left with heavy hearts’: Israel’s assault displaces thousands in Hebron

articles.title: Israel votes Tuesday in closely contested election as Netanyahu faces challenge from Eisenkot
articles.summary: Israelis head to the polls Tuesday in a closely contested parliamentary election that could end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s long rule or leave the country facing another political deadlock, with neither major bloc projected to secure a governing majority, Anadolu reports. The vote will be Israel’s first general election since the Oct. 7, 2023 attacks and the subsequent Israeli offensive on the Gaza Strip, as well as military confrontations with Lebanon and Iran. It will also be the first Israeli general election held on schedule since 1988, following decades in which successive governments collapsed before completing their four-year terms. archive.security_status_cs: Izrael dnes hlasuje v klíčových a vysoce polarizovaných parlamentních volbách, které mohou ukončit dlouholetou éru premiéra Netanjahua a přinést změnu politického kurzu. Napětí v regionu nadále zvyšují střety a operace na Západním břehu, zatímco Írán diplomaticky i vojensky manévruje vůči regionálním rivalům.
archive.security_status_en: Israel is voting today in pivotal and highly polarized parliamentary elections that could end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's long rule and shift the political course. Regional tensions remain elevated due to operations and clashes in the West Bank, while Iran continues its diplomatic and military maneuvers against regional rivals.
archive.forecast_cs: V následujících dnech se očekává vyhodnocení výsledků izraelských voleb a jejich dopad na bezpečnostní a zahraniční politiku státu. Lze předpokládat pokračující diplomatické manévry Íránu a napjatou situaci na Západním břehu.
archive.forecast_en: The coming days will focus on the outcome of the Israeli elections and their impact on state security and foreign policy. Continued Iranian diplomatic maneuvering and a tense situation in the West Bank are expected.
